messages:
ashley: kicking off canary for model v3 -> 10% traffic over 30m. want guardrails on latency, error-rate, AND token-cost. thoughts?

samir: +1 on cost. we got burned last quarter when a small prompt change doubled tokens. need an automatic pause if cost per-request > X for Y minutes.

john: agree on pause, but recommend two levels: soft-rollout-suspend (throttle new canaries) vs hard-pause (stop traffic). soft should emit events to console.

eva: telemetry question: what metric do we trust for "token-cost"? billing tokens lag. maybe use per-request tokens estimated by runtime (fast) and reconcile later with billing.

ashley: good point. use runtime-estimated-tokens for guard decisions, mark guard events as "estimated" in UI. reconciliation job can flag false-positives.

maggie: UI/UX: owners need an override button in console for "resume" with reason. also show recent prompts that triggered cost spike (sampled).

samir: on SLOs: latency SLO = P95 < 200ms for this customer class. error SLO = 0.5% 5xx. propose guard config like: 
```json
{
  "guards": [
    {"type":"latency_p95", "threshold_ms":200, "window_mins":10, "action":"pause_canary"},
    {"type":"error_rate", "threshold_pct":0.5, "window_mins":5, "action":"decrease_traffic", "new_percent":0},
    {"type":"token_cost_avg", "threshold_tokens":1200, "window_mins":15, "action":"soft_pause", "notify":"owners"}
  ]
}
```

john: API debate: should guards live as part of the Rollout resource or as separate Guard objects referenced by policy-id? Separate objects are reusable across rollouts. But embedding keeps rollout self-contained.

eva: reuse is useful for platform-level policies (enterprise accounts). maybe default to referenced Guard templates + allow overrides on rollout.

maggie: telemetry/export needs: each guard-eval should emit event with fields: rollout_id, guard_id, eval_result, sample_tokens, p95_latency_ms, action_taken, triggered_by_request_id (optional). This enables dashboarding and postmortems.

samir: automation: if token-cost guard triggers, we should probe with a lightweight sampling job to check prompt drift vs model regressions before fully pausing. acceptance test could run a 1-min sample at 1% traffic.

ashley: love the probe idea. implement a "safety-probe" action that runs for N minutes and only escalates to pause if probe fails. default probe = 2 minutes, 5% traffic.

john: small implementation note: routing layer needs to apply guard decisions synchronously for canary traffic. we'll add a guard-eval cache keyed by rollout_id -> decision TTL 1s to avoid thundering.

eva: also tie into quotas: if guard reduces traffic, make sure quota accounting doesn't abruptly free tokens and allow sudden re-expansion. throttle re-increase.

maggie: console wire: show time-series with guard thresholds overlaid, and a timeline of actions (probe, soft_pause, pause). show sample prompts inline (click to expand).

samir: can we make default numeric thresholds per-model-size? small models have different token footprints. maybe recommend table in UI.

ashley: yes. model-profile-based defaults, but owner can set absolute thresholds. Also add percent-change guards (e.g., tokens_avg increases > 40% vs baseline) to catch prompt changes.

john: open question: single guard evaluation vs composite: do we require both latency and error to trip pause or any single guard? my vote: any single severe guard should reduce traffic; only composite mild deviations should trigger probe.

eva: agree. define severity levels: severe -> immediate action, moderate -> safety-probe, mild -> notify only.

samir: ops: we need a playbook for false positives (billing reconciliation shows not actually high cost). record all manual overrides and surface to finance/owners.

maggie: also add annotation field when resuming from pause: who, why, link to investigation doc.

deploy-bot: canary deployed: rollout_id=r-8732, traffic=10%, start=1800123456. monitoring live.

ashley: ok next steps: (1) john + eva implement guard-eval API + probe runner, (2) samir hooks events to telemetry + alerting, (3) maggie wires console UI w/ resume/annotations, (4) i (PM) will draft recommended thresholds per-model and percent-change defaults.

john: will PR guard-eval API spec this afternoon.

eva: I'll add runtime-estimated-token field to request logs so guards can use it.

samir: I'll add alert rules and an initial dashboard panel for guard events.

maggie: will mock console flows and create a small usability test plan.

ashley: thanks all. leaving decision: guards default to per-rollout referenced guard-template with overrides; severity-based actions; runtime-estimated-tokens used for immediate decisions; safety-probe before hard pause. :thumbsup:

samir: :thumbsup:

maggie: :thumbsup:

john: noted, will include examples and CLI API in PR.

ashley: I'll create follow-up ticket with requirements and link this thread.

maggie: can we add a small note in the Playbook about owner-override abuse? maybe rate-limit overrides.

samir: good call. rate-limit override to 1 per 24h by default for canaries.

ashley: perfect. closing thread for now.
